chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud narrated from Abu al-Qasim Ali ibn Habashi ibn Quniyy, who said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Rawwasi, from one who narrated to him from Bashir al-Dahhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"Whoever visits him, meaning al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and performs ablution and takes a ritual bath from the Euphrates, every time he raises a foot and every time he places a foot, Allah records for him the reward of one Hajj and one Umrah."

key_terms.الْحُسَيْنُ: Imam al-Husayn, the grandson of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting Imam Husayn after purifying with Euphrates water?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith highlights the unique spiritual merit of using the waters of the Euphrates (Al-Furat) for purification before visiting Imam al-Husayn (AS), linking the physical landscape of Karbala to divine reward. It emphasizes that every step taken during this specific act of Ziyarah is counted as a complete Hajj and Umrah, underscoring the profound status of the Imam’s shrine in Shia devotional practice. This narration reflects the broader Shia tradition of valuing geographical sanctity and the tangible connection between the believer and the Ahl al-Bayt.
